info.title: AlphaStudio API
info.description:
Conventions (match the implementation exactly):
- Success responses are bare resource JSON (no envelope). Lists are `{ items, total }`.
- Errors are `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId? } }`; `code` is machine-readable and part of the contract.
- IDs are Postgres bigints serialized as decimal strings.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601.
- Every response carries `x-request-id` (echoes an inbound one).
- Auth is `Authorization: Bearer <opaque session token>`.

get.description: Liveness probe. No auth, no database access.

post.description: Creates an unverified account and emails a 6-digit verification code. Retrying with the same unverified email overwrites name/password and resends the code.
Consumes the signup code, marks the email verified, and logs the user in.
Always 204 — a silent no-op for unknown or already-verified emails.
Returns the session token, the user, and the orgs they belong to. Unverified email → 403 with details.reason = email_not_verified.
Always 204 — a silent no-op for unknown emails. Calling again resends (rate-limited). The email button links to /reset-password?email=...&code=... for autofill.

post.summary: Reset password with an emailed code
post.description: Sets the new password and revokes every existing session. Log in afterwards.
Redeems the invite code from the email (deep link /accept-invite?email=...&code=...), sets the password (and optionally the name), verifies the email, and logs in.
Revokes every session of the user, including this one.
Requires the current password. Revokes every OTHER session; this one stays valid.
The creator becomes the org's first owner. Slug is derived from the name when omitted.

get.description: The org and the caller's membership, as resolved by the tenant guard.

patch.description: Owner only. Rename and/or change the slug (duplicate slug → 409).

delete.description: Owner only. Soft-close: data is retained but every member (owners included) is locked out. Reopening requires a platform admin.

put.description: Admin or owner. Changing to a NEW country loads the org's holiday calendar from the external holidays.lookup capability and replaces the previous one (an empty result means the country has none) — expect the call to take ~10 s. Re-sending the current country succeeds immediately without a reload. Unknown/inactive country → 400; the holiday service failing → 502 with nothing changed.

post.description: Any member may leave except the last owner (409).

get.description: Accepted members only — pending invites live under /invites. Deactivated members are hidden unless ?includeInactive=true.

post.description: Admin+ only. Existing users are added immediately (informational email); new users are created and emailed a set-password code deep-linking to /accept-invite?email=...&code=....

patch.description: Owner only. The last owner cannot be demoted (409).

delete.description: Admins may remove members; owners may remove anyone but the last owner. Soft-remove — re-inviting reactivates. Self-removal must use POST .../leave.

get.description: Admin+ only. Invites the recipient has not accepted yet.

post.description: Admin+ only. Mints a fresh code and re-sends the email. Rate-limited (429).

delete.description: Admin+ only. Deletes the pending membership; if the invitee has no other org, their placeholder account and codes are deleted too. Accepted invites → 409 (remove the member instead).

get.description: Proxy to the AlphaProStudio service `GET /v1/wallet` for this org's tenant — the response is the upstream's, passed through. `availableCents` is what the next generation request is checked against. New orgs are funded automatically on creation; there is no client-facing funding endpoint. Upstream down → 502.

Proxy to the AlphaProStudio service `GET /v1/usage` — the response is the upstream's, passed through. `from`/`to` are inclusive UTC days (YYYY-MM-DD); `group_by` is model | tenant | capability (default model). `model` and `capability` report the org's own usage; `tenant` reports across every org of this app (the upstream's cross-tenant billing view). A backwards or >400-day window → 400; upstream down → 502.

Proxy to the AlphaProStudio service `GET /v1/catalog/capabilities/:capability` — the response is the upstream's, passed through: which model aliases the capability may run on and whether the plan choice is the caller's at all (`selectable: false` = the capability pins its model). Ask plainly for every reachable model, or with `?plan=` for the row that grade would render on. An unknown or not-granted capability → 404 (the upstream answers both identically); a plan the catalog does not have → 400; upstream down → 502.

post.description: Proxy to `POST /v1/run/tones.preview` — SYNC: the finished run comes back inline with one sample line in `outputs[0].content.sample`, for the tone editor. The body is frontend-owned and forwards verbatim: `tone` travels inline (required upstream); `brandVoice` is optional — send it and it is authoritative, omit it and the platform reads the org's pushed context bundle. Expect a few seconds.

Proxy to `POST /v1/run/social-posts.generate` — BATCH: answers 202 `{ runId, status: 'queued' }`; the judged, grounded drafts are pullable via `GET .../posts/runs/:runId` (a run reaches `completed` within a couple of seconds). The body is frontend-owned and forwards verbatim: 1–3 inline `tones` (unique ids), `plan` picks the whole recipe, `attachedEvent.rules` (the holidays.lookup shape) outrank tone and brand rules. Over-budget fan-out (tones × perTone > 6) or duplicate tone ids → 400.

get.description: Proxy to `GET /v1/runs/:runId` — status + outputs for a run this org started (`queued → running → completed | failed`). Also how a result is recovered when a callback was missed: the run record is terminal and pullable regardless of delivery. Model steps name the app's own aliases — no vendor ref ever appears. Unknown run, or another org's → 404.

post.description: Proxy to `POST /v1/media/jobs` — ONE endpoint whose body shape the FRONTEND decides: the body's `capability` field (default media.generate) selects the schema the upstream parses it with; everything passes through verbatim. 202 `{ jobId, status: 'queued' }` — balanced renders settle in seconds, dearer plans finish later; poll the job. The org's wallet pays: an estimate the wallet cannot cover → 402 wallet_insufficient. A retired `modelAlias` field → 400 (send `plan`).

get.description: Proxy to `GET /v1/media/jobs`, newest first. Assets are listed WITHOUT presigned urls — mint one via `POST .../media/assets/:assetId/presign` for the ones you open.

Proxy to `GET /v1/media/jobs/:jobId` — the polling endpoint. Assets on a finished job arrive WITH presigned GET urls (1 h) already minted. No provider or vendor model ref ever appears. Unknown job, or another org's → 404.

post.description: Proxy to `POST /v1/media/assets/presign` — the org's OWN image, in (for reference-image capabilities like images.edit). Returns an assetId and a presigned PUT; send the bytes there with exactly the requested mediaType. A mediaType outside png/jpeg/webp → 400. Nothing is generated or metered.

post.summary: Presign a media asset for download
post.description: Proxy to `POST /v1/media/assets/:assetId/presign` (no body) — a presigned, expiring GET over an asset this org owns; this is what goes into `params.referenceImages`. The read IS the ownership check: unknown and not-yours are the same 404, on purpose.

delete.description: Proxy to `DELETE /v1/media/assets/:assetId`: removes an asset this org owns — a render output or an upload — deleting the object and the row together. Unknown or not-yours → 404.

post.description: Proxy to `POST /v1/rag/collections`. A collection pins ONE embedding model alias and ONE chunk profile for its lifetime. `scope: tenant` = only this org sees it; `app` = every org of this app. A name already used in the scope, or an alias the app does not hold → 400. Unknown fields pass through to the upstream schema.

get.description: Proxy to `GET /v1/rag/collections`: every collection this org can see — its own, plus every collection created with `scope: app`. Another org's collections are not listed and are 404 by id.

Proxy to `GET /v1/rag/collections/:collectionId/sources`: every source with its ingestion state (`Uploading → Processing → Ready | Failed`). A presigned upload that was never PUT stays visible as `Uploading`. Unknown collection → 404.

post.summary: Add a source to a collection
post.description: Proxy to `POST /v1/rag/collections/:collectionId/sources` — two body shapes on `kind`: `push` (send `content` you already have, with `title`/`mediaType`) or `url` (an http/https URL the platform fetches under its SSRF rules). 202, not 200: ingestion is asynchronous — the source comes back `Processing`; poll it or watch the sources list. Unknown collection → 404.

Proxy to `POST /v1/rag/collections/:collectionId/sources/presign`. Step 1 of an upload: the source row exists as `Uploading` the moment this returns. PUT the bytes to `uploadUrl` with EXACTLY the requested `mediaType` (it is part of the signature); ingestion starts by itself when the object lands — there is no 'complete' call. Presigns live 15 minutes. Media types the platform cannot extract (e.g. image/png) → 400.

get.description: Proxy to `GET /v1/rag/sources/:sourceId` — poll this to watch ingestion settle. `failureReason` appears only on `Failed` and comes from a closed vocabulary, never a stack trace. Unknown source, or another org's → 404.

delete.description: Proxy to `DELETE /v1/rag/sources/:sourceId`. Vectors are removed inline, BEFORE this returns — `vectorsDeleted` makes that checkable. Deleting an already-deleted source → 404. Unlike the rest of this API, a successful delete answers 200 with a body, not 204 — the upstream's shape is passed through.

delete.description: Hard delete — brand resources have no soft-delete flag. Also refreshes the org's AlphaProStudio context bundle server-side (best-effort; a failed refresh never fails the write).

delete.description: Unknown rule, a rule of another voice, or a voice of another org → 404. Also refreshes the org's AlphaProStudio context bundle server-side (best-effort; a failed refresh never fails the write).

get.description: Calendar order (date ascending), offset-paginated. The calendar is loaded when the org's country is set (PUT /orgs/:orgId/country) and empty until then. Read-only — holidays are replaced wholesale by a country change, never edited here.
The caller's own inbox for this org, newest first. Offset-paginated, 50 per page by default.
Badge count — notifications with no seenAt.

post.summary: Mark all my notifications as read
post.description: Idempotent — calling it again reports `updated: 0`.

get.description: Newest first, offset-paginated. Scoped to the org in the path.

post.description: `toneIds` must all be tones of this org — an unknown or foreign id is a 400 naming it.

get.description: Unknown id, or one belonging to another org → 404.

patch.description: Partial update — send only the fields that change (at least one). `toneIds` replaces the whole selection; `[]` clears it.

delete.description: Hard delete — the tone selection goes with it.

get.description: Active countries, name-ordered — the valid values for an event source's `country`. Global reference data: the same list for every org, and not paginated.
Newest first, offset-paginated. Scoped to the org in the path.

post.description: `country` must be an active country (see /countries). One source per kind + country — a duplicate is a 409.

get.description: Unknown id, or one belonging to another org → 404.

patch.description: Partial update — send only the fields that change (at least one). Colliding with an existing kind + country is a 409.

delete.description: Hard delete — the slots it produced are deleted with it.

get.description: Calendar order (date ascending), offset-paginated. Filter with from/to (inclusive), status and eventSourceId.

patch.description: The only slot mutation: `skip: true` sets status `skipped`, `skip: false` puts it back to `review`. Slots are created by event ingestion, never by clients.

post.description: Accepts any JSON payload from an external sender and acknowledges it. No auth — external services cannot hold a session token.
